I think that at least is more because Argent's deck seems to almost entirely take place a little bit before he encountered the Naturalist. The latest Virtuoso of the Void issue in Argent's deck is #21, while the card in Naturalist's deck with Argent trying to help his gazelle form use its senses better is Virtuoso of the Void #24.

Other issues in Argent's deck seem to mostly reference his origin (Toll of Destiny presumably is about that) or his first adventures with the Prime Wardens (#17 is the latest issue while the events of OblivAeon were in the 50s, for comparison.)

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
I maintain that we don't have enough information to make judgements.  I mean, who encounters a person who their enemy turned into an antelope, and their first response is, "I know!  I'll turn them into a rhinocerous!"  Clearly there are extra limitations or circumstances that we are unaware of.

 

Off the top of my head, possible reasons:

If Drake sticks around too long, he risks Akash'bhuta noticing and turning the Naturalist into a frog.
The Naturalist's company built a bypass through Drake's bar, and he's doing his duty despite wishing he could let the guy rot.
Drake wasn't actually present - this was a dream quest or something, and he just woke up.
Drake actually spent several hours with him, but he didn't remember because he was a rhinocerous.

 

I don't think that any of those are particularly likely.  My point is that there are lots of reasons that Drake's behavior might be justified if we saw his side of the story.  Or maybe he's just a jerk.

phantaskippy:

Fugue State Parse is definitely a "Leader Tier" hero.Leader Tier is the name we have given to heroes that drastically alter the balance of power, with very little card luck reliance.  She'r right up there with the Legacies, FV Bunker, Team Leader Tachyon and Dark Visionary.We usually save them for really tough fights or revenge beatdowns. I can't wait for Parse, she's amazing.I will never forget the infamous "Parse is the worst hero ever" thread.  I won't say anymore.

 

The Legacies, TL Tachyon and Dark Visionary, I all totally agree on, but how does FV Bunker serve as a balance-of-power adjuster, though?  Destroying Ongoings is nice, but there are plenty of heroes who, through a combination of card draw and deck balance, have almost-as-good ongoing destruction (Visionary, Nightmist, Wraith, Tachyon, Guise).  Essentially, FV Bunker needs to draw a Mode card to destroy an Ongoing destruction – how is that much different from (ex:) Nightmist needing to draw Planar Banishment, or Guise needing to draw Retcon?  Yes, he's got a few more Modes in his deck than they do, but Planar Banishment and Retcon can take out ongoings or environments, and both Nightmist and Guise have enough card-drawing abilities that it usually doesn't take long to get the card in their hand.
